text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Women occupy seven percent of Vietnam's ministerial posts compared with a regional average of four percent, says the United Nations Children Fund.
-- Vietnam and the United States have exchanged the draft of an aviation agreement, for reference before the official start of negotiations.
-- The Ministry of Health has requested hospitals acroos the country to limit imports of medical equipment manufactured before 1995.

-- Laos and Burma will make important contributions to the common values of ASEAN as well as the political and economic potentials of the association, Vietnam's Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam said on Wednesday.

-- Vietnam's paper industry is facing an oversupply crisis with some 20,000 tonnes of paper in stock at the end of June and consumption equalling only 90 percent of total output. The government has issued a decision to limit imports of paper.
-- The Ho Chi Minh City People's Committee has called for greater efforts to improve the lives of market inspectors whose average income is just $25 per month.
